Note that the factor $2\sqrt{{x}^{2}+9}$ is always positive for all real numbers $x.$

Since $2\sqrt{{x}^{2}+9}$ is always positive, we can divide both sides of the inequality by this quantity. By doing this, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(2\sqrt{{x}^{2}+9})(-7x-5)}{\,2\sqrt{{x}^{2}+9}\,} & <\frac{0}{\,2\sqrt{{x}^{2}+9}\,} \\ -7x-5 & <0 \\ -7x & <5 \\ x & >\,-\frac{5}{7}.\end{aligned}
$$
